title: 𒀭𒂗𒆠 𒉣
titleEn: Laws of Hammurabi — Epilogue III: the curses of Ea, Šamaš, Sîn and Adad (xlii 98 – xliii 80)
part: Epilogue III · the curses of Ea, Šamaš, Sîn and Adad (Col. xlii 98 – xliii 80)
draftNote: The § chips number the laws (Harper’s sectioning, still standard); long laws span several tap-units. Readings checked sign-by-sign against Harper’s 1904 edition.
source: Louvre stele, after R.F. Harper, The Code of Hammurabi, King of Babylon (Chicago, 1904): transliteration and autograph plates, List of Signs. Readings are Harper’s in modern subscript notation. Cuneiform in Old Babylonian monumental sign forms via the SantakkuM webfont by Sylvie Vanséveren (CC BY 4.0); pronunciation: conventional reconstructed Old Babylonian. Audio: a German synthetic voice reads the Akkadian word by word from these pronunciation rules (word stress after Huehnergard). It cannot hold a consonant long, so doubled consonants are heard single (šumma with one m), and the emphatics ṭ and q are heard as plain t and k. Fresh translations made directly from the Akkadian; Harper’s public-domain translation consulted for sense only.

about: The third part of the epilogue goes on with the curses on a later king who destroys or alters the stele, each god taking a turn. Ea, the great prince who knows everything and lengthens the king’s days, is asked to turn wisdom and understanding away from the wrongdoer, to bring him to oblivion, to block his rivers at the source, and to keep Ašnan, the grain, the life of the people, from growing in his land (xlii 98 – xliii 13). Šamaš, great judge of heaven and earth, is asked to overthrow his kingship, to leave his case unjudged, to confuse his path, to destroy the foundation of his army, to set a bad omen in his sight, to let the grievous word of Šamaš overtake him quickly, to uproot him from among the living and to deprive his spirits of water in the earth (xliii 14–40). Sîn, lord of heaven, is asked to take away crown and throne, to lay on him a heavy guilt that will not vanish in his body, to end his reign in sighing and tears and to decree for him a life like death (xliii 41–63). Adad, lord of abundance, is asked to take away the rain and the flood-water, to destroy his land with famine and hunger, to storm against his city and to turn his land into a mound of the flood (xliii 64–80, which runs on into the next part). The stele is read through Harper’s 1904 transliteration and his plates; the readings of a number of verbs are his and uncertain, and the notes say which.

sentences.i: Ea, the great prince, whose destinies go in front,
sentences.n: A new god is called, and a new paragraph of curses begins. Ea is written {d}EN.KI, as in epilogue-1. rubûm “prince” is the single sign NUN (Harper’s glossary lists RUBÛ [NUN] at this very line); ra-bi-um is syllabic rabûm “great”. ša šīmātūšu is “whose fates”, šīmtum (plural šīmātum, as in mušīm šīmātim, xlii 53) + -šu. ina maḫra illakā is “in front they go”: illakā is the present of alākum, 3rd feminine plural, agreeing with šīmātūšu; maḫra is Harper’s maḫru “front, before”. The picture, a god whose destinies lead the way, is Harper’s sense and the exact force of ina maḫra is UNCERTAIN.

sentences.i: the leader of the gods, who knows everything there is, who lengthens
sentences.n: abkal ilī “leader of the gods”. abkal is the two signs NUN.ME (Harper’s glossary ABKALLU “wise one, leader” [NUN.ME], at this line; on the plate NUN is the hatched sign with its upright wedge, then ME), and ilī is the doubled sign NI.NI, as at xlii 22. mūdi mimma šumšu is the phrase of the litany, “who knows whatever its name”, that is, everything. mušarriku is the Š participle of arākum “to be long” (Harper’s arāku III,1), “who lengthens”; what he lengthens stands at the top of the next column (xliii 1), so this unit ends mid-sentence, as the column does. The final -u is a nominative vowel kept in the construct, as in mušarbû (xlii 57).

sentences.i: the days of my life; may he turn understanding and wisdom away from him, and
sentences.n: ūm balāṭīya “the days of my life” is the object of mušarriku at the end of the last column. ūm is written UD-um (Harper’s glossary ÛMU lists UD-um at this line), the construct form “day(s) of”; balāṭīya is balāṭum “life” + -ia “my” (Harper’s balāṭu). Then a new wish, with the verb last: uznam u nēmeqam litēršuma. uznum is “ear”, and by extension “understanding” (the accusative, uz-na-am on the plate: UZ, NA, AM); nēmeqam is “wisdom” (nemēqum, as in epilogue-1; the GA sign is read qa₂). litēršuma is the precative of the D-stem of târum + -šu + -ma “and”, rendered as in epilogue-2 (“let him turn away from him”); that sense is UNCERTAIN, as there.

sentences.n: The next god, Šamaš (the sign UTU). dajjānum rabûm is “the great judge” (syllabic, as Harper’s glossary lists it at this line); ša šamê u erṣetim “of heaven and earth”. muštēšir is the Št participle of ešērum “to be straight” (the same verb as šutēšurum in the litany), “who guides aright”, here written mu-uš-te-še-ir. šaknāt napištim is literally “those set (with) life”: šaknāt, from šakānum “to set, place”, feminine plural, + napištim “of life”; it is read as “those who have life”, UNCERTAIN in its grammar. bēlum tukulti is read “the lord, my trust”, UNCERTAIN: the title stands alone after the string of epithets. be-lum is the full nominative, not the construct bēl that this text writes in be-el šamê (xliii 41) and be-el ḫegallim (xliii 64), so it does not govern tukulti; and the other gods’ epithets close the same way, with a “my” noun (ilum bānî “the god, my creator”, rēṣūa “my helper”), so tu-kul-ti is taken as tukultī, the suffix -ī not written out. The alternative, the construct chain bēl tukulti “lord of trust”, is possible if the -um is a slip. tukultu is Harper’s “strength” (his glossary has tu-kul-ti at this line, without a suffix), modern “support, reliance”; “trust” is my choice; the GUL sign is read kul (Harper’s list no. 164).

sentences.i: may he overthrow his kingship; may he not judge his case; may he confuse his path; may he destroy the foundation of his army,
sentences.n: Four wishes, each ending in its verb. šarrūssu liskip: šarrūssu is šarrūtum + -šu (t + š said ss, written ZU, as in epilogue-2), liskip the precative of sakāpum “to overthrow” (Harper’s sakâpu). dīnšu ay idīn: dīnum “case” + -šu, ay “may not”, idīn the preterite of diānum (Harper’s dânu) “to judge”: “may he not judge his case”. urḫušu liši: urḫum “path” (Harper’s urḫu) + -šu; liši is Harper’s ešû “to confuse, cause to err”, UNCERTAIN in form and sense. išid ummānišu lišḫelṣi: išid is the sign SUḪUŠ “foundation” (Harper’s išid, as in the glossary at this line), ummānišu “his army”, and lišḫelṣi, Harper’s ḫalṣû III,1 “to destroy”, the Š precative of ḫalāṣum (UNCERTAIN; the sign ZI is read ṣi). sentences.n: agâm kussâm ša šarrūtim: “the crown, the throne of kingship”, two accusatives side by side; litēršu as at xliii 4. UNCERTAIN, the signs: Harper normalises the two words as agâm and kussâm and prints no hyphens (the scan of his page is washed out here). His glossary gives “crown” at this line as a Sumerogram (AGÛ [MIR], while the litany’s a-gi-im is syllabic), so agâm is one logogram sign, keyed AGA₃ (the sign of AGA₃.ÚS in laws-26-41); its identification with the first sign-group of the tall row is TENTATIVE (the group has the outline of the first sign of Harper’s List no. 135, agû). kussâm is {giš}GU.ZA as in laws-1-10 (Harper’s glossary kussû [IŠ.GU.ZA]); the plate’s upper tier has four sign-groups, the first for agâm and the next three for GIŠ, GU, ZA, which I could match with Harper’s List no. 108 (kussû) only in outline. The raised mark before ša, which in the washed-out scan looks like a footnote 1, is Harper’s raised b, and the plate shows what it means: line 45 is a tall row of two tiers, and ša šar-ru-tim stands on the lower.

D-stem of târum: to give back: turru “taken away/captured”; utarrūšumma “they shall return (it) to him” · utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · turrim (infinitive, tu-ur-ri-im): ana turrim “for repaying, to give back”; utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · uttēr (ut-te-ir, perfect) “he has given back”: the same verb as utâr · litēršu (li-te-ir-šu, precative + -šu, Harper’s taru II,1) “let him turn back / take back from him”, UNCERTAIN: melam šarrūtim litēršu “let him turn the glory of kingship away from him” · litēr (li-te-ir, precative, without a suffix) “let him turn”: ana tīl abūbim litēr “let him turn (it) into a mound of the flood”

sentences.i: may he turn his land into a mound of the flood.
sentences.n: The last unit of the part. mātassu ana tīl abūbim litēr: tīl abūbim “mound of the flood” (Harper’s telu “hill, heap”, written til with the BAD sign; abūbum “the flood”, the Deluge; Harper’s glossary has ABUBU “hurricane”, the flood being the modern sense), the mound of ruins left by a flood; litēr is the D precative of târum “to turn”, here with ana, “let him turn into”. The sentence of curses of Adad goes on in the next part.

glossary.Sin: Sin ({d}EN.ZU) — the moon-god, patron of Ur
glossary.abkallum: wise one, leader (Harper’s abkallu, written NUN.ME): abkal ilī “leader of the gods” (abkal the form before a genitive; ilī written NI.NI)
glossary.abūbum: the flood, the Deluge (Harper’s ABUBU, glossed by him “hurricane”; the flood is the modern sense): abūbim (a-bu-bi-im, genitive) “of the flood”
glossary.agûm: crown · written with one logogram AGA₃ (the sign of AGA₃.ÚS in laws-26-41) at XLIII 45, agâm (accusative) “the crown”, the sign TENTATIVE; the litany spells it syllabically a-gi-im
glossary.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law · alākišu (a-la-ki-šu) “his going” (infinitive with -šu): ina alākišu “in his going” · Gt present ittallak (it-ta-al-la-ak) “she shall go away” (the Gt gives the sense of going off; the Gtn would be ittanallak) · ittalak “she has gone” (perfect): ana šīmtim ittalak “she has gone to her fate” · ittalku (it-ta-al-ku) with the subjunctive -u: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate” · ittalkamma (it-ta-al-kam-ma) perfect ittalkam (ittalak + the ventive -am, “hither”) “he has come”, + -ma “and” · lillikma (li-il-li-ik-ma, li- + illik + -ma) “let him go, and” · illakā (i-la-ka) “they go”, present 3rd feminine plural, agreeing with a feminine plural noun: ša šīmātūšu ina maḫra illakā “whose fates go in front”
glossary.ana: to, for · with an infinitive, “to, for” (ana kirîm zaqāpim “to plant as an orchard”); “as” (ana kirîm), “into” (ana libbi), “at the rate of” (ana itêšu) · also “over” (ana ālīya “over my city”), “before” in ana maḫar “into the presence of”; of time, ana dār “for ever”, ana warki “hereafter”, ana matīma “whenever”; ana lā + infinitive “so as not to”
glossary.arākum-Š: Š-stem of arākum “to be long”: to lengthen, make long · mušarriku (mu-ša-ri-ku, Š participle, Harper’s arāku III,1) “who lengthens”; the final -u is a nominative vowel kept in the construct
glossary.arḫiš: quickly, speedily (adverb in -iš, Harper’s arḫiš): ar-ḫi-iš
glossary.awātum: word, statement, matter · awâtim (a-wa-a-tim, plural genitive) “of words”: ana awâtim “to the words” · awâtīya (a-wa-ti-ia) and awâtūa (a-wa-tu-u-a) “my words” (plural + -ia) · awāssu (a-wa-zu, with -šu “his”, the ss written ZU) “his word”
glossary.ay: may not, let not (the negative-wish particle, Harper’s a “prohibitive”; written a, said ay), before a preterite: ay unakkir “may he not change”, ay ušazziq “may he not efface”, ay iršiā “may they not get”; it is not lā
glossary.balāṭum: to live; D-stem bulluṭum — muballiṭ “who gives life” · stative baltat (ba-al-ṭa-at) “she lives”, in adi baltat “as long as she lives” · the noun “life”: balāṭam (ba-la-ṭam, accusative) “a life”; balāṭīya (ba-la-ṭi-ia) “my life”; ūm balāṭīya “the days of my life”
glossary.balṭum: alive, living (Harper’s baltu): balṭūtim (ba-al-tu-tim, genitive plural, TU written for ṭu) “among the living”; ina balṭūtim
glossary.bašûm-Š: Š-stem of bašûm “to exist”: to bring into being, produce (a crop): uštabši “he has produced” (perfect) · uštabši (uš-tab-ši) “he has brought about” (perfect): kazzatam uštabši “he has brought about a harm (?)” · ušabšû (u-ša-ab-šu-u) “which he brought about” (preterite + relative -u) · šubšâm (šu-ub-ša-a-am, Š infinitive, accusative) “to bring into being”: lā šubšâm “not to bring into being”, Harper’s basu III,1 (su-ub-sa-a-am), with no sense given by him · ušabši (u-ša-ab-ši, preterite 3rd singular, after ay) “(may he not) bring into being”: ay ušabši
glossary.bubūtum: hunger (Harper’s bûbûtu): bubūtim (bu-bu-tim, genitive) “of hunger”; ina ḫušaḫḫim u bubūtim “with famine and hunger”
glossary.bānûm: creator; bānîšu “his creator” · builder (ŠITIM): bānûm “the builder”, bānîm šuāti “of that builder”, one who builds a house; the sign Harper numbers 168 is keyed ŠITIM tentatively, UNCERTAIN
glossary.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard” · bēl (be-el), the construct “owner of”, also with a suffix on the noun that follows: bēl ḫubullišu “his creditor”, bēl ḫubulliša “her creditor” · bēl (be-el, not the sign EN) “owner of”: bēl aššatim “the owner of the wife”, i.e. the man entitled to her (my reading) · bēlišu (be-li-šu) “its owner” (of an animal), bēlišuma “to its owner only” (with the emphatic -ma); bēl alpim “the owner of the ox” · bēl epinnim “the owner of the plough”, bēl tarbaṣim “the owner of the pen”; bēlīšunu (be-li-šu-nu) “their owners”, the owners of the cattle and sheep a herdsman has lost · bēl (be-el) “owner of” before a genitive: bēl wardim “the owner of the male slave” · bēlī (be-li) “my master”: ul bēlī atta “you are not my master” · bēlšu, bēlišu (be-el-šu, be-li-šu) “his master” · bēlum (be-lum, the full nominative, not the construct bēl) “the lord”, standing alone as a title after epithets: bēlum tukultī “the lord, my trust”, UNCERTAIN
glossary.bīrum: sight, vision (Harper’s bīru): bīrišu (bi-ri-šu) “his sight”; ina bīrišu “in his sight”
glossary.dimmatum: tears, weeping, lament: dimmatim (di-im-ma-tim, genitive) “of weeping”; ina tanēḫim u dimmatim “in sighing and weeping”
glossary.diānum: to judge: dīnam idīn “he judged a case” · adīnu (a-di-nu) “I judged” (first person preterite + relative -u, filed by Harper under dânum “to judge”; the same word was read addinu, nadānum, in the part before): dīn adīnu “the verdict I judged” · lidīn (li-di-in, precative) “let him judge”
glossary.dīnum: case, lawsuit; judgment: dīn napištim “a case of life” · dīnāt (di-na-a-at, plural, the form before a genitive) “judgments of”; dīn mātim “the case of the land”
glossary.ekimmum: spirit of the dead, ghost (Harper’s ekimmu, written GEKIM; modern GIDIM): the doubled sign GIDIM.GIDIM marks the plural, ekimmêšu (GIDIM.GIDIM-šu) “his spirits”; the sign identification is TENTATIVE
glossary.eli: against, upon · with suffixes: elišu, eliša, elišunu “upon him, her, them” (of a debt)
glossary.elîš: above (adverb in -iš, from elûm “up”): elîš (e-li-iš); with šaplîš “below”, together “everywhere”
glossary.emēdum: to lay on, impose; with arnam, arnam emēdum “to lay guilt (on oneself)”, i.e. to be in the wrong (Harper emēdu I,1): immidū (i-im-mi-du) “they have laid (guilt), they are in the wrong” (preterite, 3rd plural; the -u is the plural ending, the doubled m is the assimilated d of the root, spelled out in the sign mi); the whole sense of the clause, “the sons are in the wrong”, rests on this reading and is UNCERTAIN in its grammar · limussuma (li-mu-zu-ma, li- + the verb + -šu + -ma) “let him lay upon him, and” (Harper’s emēdu II,1, a D-stem); the vowel u of the spelling is not explained, so the form is UNCERTAIN
glossary.erṣetum: earth, land, territory: erṣetišunu “their territory” · erṣetim (ir-ṣi-tim, genitive) “of earth”: šamê u erṣetim “of heaven and earth”, ina erṣetim “in the earth” · erṣetīšu (ir-ṣi-ti-šu) “his land”
glossary.ezzum: furious, raging (Harper’s ezzu, adverb ezziš “furiously”) · izziš (iz-zi-iš, with i for e, adverb in -iš) “furiously”
glossary.ešûm: to confuse, cause to err (Harper’s ešû I,1; a base sense “to be confused, go astray” is inferred): liši (li-ši) “let him confuse”, UNCERTAIN in form and sense
glossary.ešērum-Št: Št-stem of ešērum “to be straight”: to guide aright · muštēšir (mu-uš-te-še-ir, Št participle) “who guides”; the same verb as šutēšurum in the litany
glossary.gugallum: regent (Harper’s gugallu, syllabic gu-gal), the title of the god who oversees the canals; modern editions take it as “canal-inspector”: gugal šamê u erṣetim “the regent of heaven and earth”
glossary.ilum: god; here: the temple as owner · plural ilāni “gods” (written DINGIR.DINGIR, as in the litany): maḫar ilāni “before the gods” · ilum (the AN sign alone, DINGIR) “the god”, the god not named in the line · ilī (written NI.NI, two triangle signs, Harper’s List no. 99) “gods”: irrīt ilī “the curse of the gods”, abu ilī “father of the gods”
glossary.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”) · “through, by (means of)”: ina maḫāṣim “through beating”, ina pilšim “by a breach”; “regarding”: ina mimma ša … “regarding whatever …”; ina šanat “in the year” · “with, by”, of company or means (UNCERTAIN): ina liātim “with (or by) the cattle” · also “with, by means of” (ina kakkim dannim “with the mighty weapon”, ina igigallim “with wisdom”), “by” with kibīt “command” and awāt “word” (the authority), “in” a manner (ina damiqtim “in favor”, ina šulmim “in peace”)
glossary.itti: with · “from”, after leqûm “to take”: itti šarrāqānišu ileqqi “from his thief he shall take” · itti mārīšu “among his sons” (it-ti, written IT, the sign A₂, and TI): the sense “among, in the number of”, after manûm “to count”
glossary.išdum: foundation (written with the single sign SUḪUŠ)
glossary.kabtum: heavy; grave (of an offence): arnam kabtam (kab-tam, accusative) “a heavy offence” · of a wound, severe: ṣimmam kabtam (kab-tam, accusative) “a severe wound”
glossary.kammalum: burden, ignominy (Harper’s kammalu): kammal (kam-ma-al, the form before a genitive) “the burden of”: kammal šarrūtim “the burden of kingship”
glossary.kašādum: to reach, overcome: iktašassu “(the River) has overcome him” · likšussu (li-ik-šu-zu, precative + -šu, the d and š said ss, written ZU) “let it reach him, overtake him”
glossary.kussûm: chair, seat ({giš}GU.ZA) — the seat of office · kussâm (accusative) “the throne”: agâm kussâm ša šarrūtim “the crown, the throne of kingship”
glossary.lemnum: evil, bad: lemnam (lim-nam, accusative) “an evil omen”
glossary.lā: not (in subordinate and nominal contexts) · before a noun in the genitive, “without”: lā kanīkim “without a sealed receipt”; in a šumma-clause, “not”: lā ītamar “he did not see” · before an infinitive, ana lā ḫabālim “so as not to wrong”
glossary.marūštum: grievous, blighting (Harper’s marūštu): marūštum (ma-ru-uš-tum, feminine nominative) “grievous”, of a word (awātum)
glossary.maḫrum: front, before (Harper’s maḫru): ina maḫra (maḫ-ra) “in front”, of fates that go before a god; the exact force UNCERTAIN
glossary.mišītum: oblivion, forgetting (Harper’s mišîtu): mišītim (mi-ši-tim, genitive after ina) “in oblivion”
glossary.mû: water(s); mê nuḫšim “waters of abundance” · ina mêšu (ME-e-šu) “in his waters”, of a child taken while in the waters of birth, i.e. perhaps a newborn, the idiom UNCERTAIN; the form mê is the oblique of a plural-looking noun
glossary.mātum: land, country · māt (ma-at) the form before a following genitive, “the land of”: ina māt nukurtim “in a hostile country” · mātim (ma-tim, or the Sumerogram KALAM, no ending written) genitive “of the land”: ina libbu mātim “in the middle of the land”, mārū mātim “natives of the country”, mātim šanītim “another country” · mātassu (ma-zu, with -šu “his”, the t and š said ss and written with ZU) “his land”; mātišu (ma-ti-šu) “his land”
glossary.mīlum: flood, high water (Harper’s “water-flood”): mīlam (mi-lam, accusative) “the flood”
glossary.mūdûm: one who knows: šībī mūdi ḫulqišu “witnesses who know his lost property”; mūdûssunu “what they know”
glossary.mūtum: death (mūtum; not mutum “husband”): mūt (mu-ut, the form before a genitive) “death of”
glossary.nasāḫum: to pull out, uproot; of a son, to cast out, disinherit (Harper: “to cut off, to disinherit”): nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im, infinitive) “to cast out”; anassaḫ (a-na-za-aḫ) “I shall cast out” (first person present); inassaḫ (i-na-za-aḫ) “he shall cast out” (third person present) · inassaḫū (i-na-za-ḫu) “they shall pluck out”, present plural: īnšu inassaḫū “they shall pluck out his eye” (the ZA sign for sa) · nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im) infinitive “to cast out”: ana tarbītim nasāḫim “to cast out the foster-child” · assuḫ (az-zu-uḫ, preterite, 1st person) “I tore out”, of enemies · lissuḫ (li-zu-uḫ, precative, the n assimilated and the ss written with ZU) “let him uproot”: raggam u ṣēnam lissuḫ “let him uproot the wicked and the evil one” · nasāḫ (na-sa-aḫ, infinitive in the construct) “the uprooting of”: nasāḫ išid šarrūtišu “the uprooting of the foundation of his kingship” · lissuḫšu (li-iz-zu-uḫ-šu, precative + -šu, the n assimilated, ZU for ss) “let him uproot him”
glossary.nemēqum: wisdom, skill (Harper’s nemequ): nemēqīya (ne-me-qi₂-ia) “my wisdom” (KI read qi₂)
glossary.nisûm: to break loose, storm (Harper’s nisû I,1) · lissima (li-is-si-ma, li- + the verb + -ma “and”) “let him storm, and”; the verb is UNCERTAIN
glossary.nišū: people; the household: nišīšu “his household” · nišīšu (ni-ši-šu) “his people”: nišīšu ina mīšarim lirʾi “let him shepherd his people in justice”; šīr nišīšu “the flesh of his people”
glossary.nārum: river (written ÍD; the doubled sign ÍD.ÍD marks the plural): nārātum “rivers” · nārātīšu (ÍD.ÍD-šu) “his rivers”
glossary.palûm: reign, term of rule (the BAL sign, Harper’s List no. 7, palû): palêya (BALA-ia, with -ia “my”) “my reign” · palê (BALA, before a genitive) “the reign of”: palê tanēḫim “a reign of sighing”
glossary.qatûm-Š: Š-stem of qatûm “to come to an end” (Harper’s qatû III,1): to bring to an end, cut off · lišaqti (li-ša-aq-ti, Š precative; AK read aq) “let him bring to an end”
glossary.rabûm: great; D/Š-stems “make great”; rabûtim “great (pl.)” · rabîtim (ra-bi-tim, feminine genitive) “large”: ina abnim rabîtim “by the large stone” · rabītišu (ra-bi-ti-šu) “his senior one”, the feminine with -šu: read as the father’s chief wife, UNCERTAIN
glossary.sakāpum: to overthrow (Harper’s sakâpu): liskip (li-is-ki-ip, precative) “let him overthrow”
glossary.sekērum: to shut off, block (Harper’s sakâru, glossed by him “to dam up”): liskir (li-is-ki-ir, precative) “let him block”
glossary.tanēḫum: sighing, groaning (Harper’s taneḫu): tanēḫim (ta-ne-ḫi-im, genitive) in palê tanēḫim “a reign of sighing”
glossary.tukultum: trust, support (Harper’s tukultu, glossed by him “strength”): tukultī (tu-kul-ti, the suffix -ī “my” not written out) “my trust”, UNCERTAIN; the GUL sign is read kul
glossary.târum: to return: ul itârma “he shall never again …” · itâr (i-ta-ar) “he shall go back”: ana bīt abišu itâr “he shall go back to his father’s house” · littarrūšu (li-it-ta-ar-ru-šu, li- + a t-stem form + -šu, Harper’s târu I,2, the Gt) “let him bring him”, UNCERTAIN in form (the ending -ū looks plural, “let them”?) and in sense: mišītim littarrūšu “bring him to oblivion”
glossary.târum-D: D-stem of târum: to give back: turru “taken away/captured”; utarrūšumma “they shall return (it) to him” · utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · turrim (infinitive, tu-ur-ri-im): ana turrim “for repaying, to give back”; utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · uttēr (ut-te-ir, perfect) “he has given back”: the same verb as utâr · litēršu (li-te-ir-šu, precative + -šu, Harper’s taru II,1) “let him turn back / take back from him”, UNCERTAIN: melam šarrūtim litēršu “let him turn the glory of kingship away from him” · litēr (li-te-ir, precative, without a suffix) “let him turn”: ana tīl abūbim litēr “let him turn (it) into a mound of the flood”
glossary.tīlum: mound, heap of ruins (Harper’s telu “hill, heap”): til (written with the BAD sign) in tīl abūbim “a mound of the flood”
glossary.ummānum: army, host: ummānišu (um-ma-ni-šu) “his army”; išid ummānišu “the foundation of his army”
glossary.uznum: ear: uznašu (written u-zu-un-šu, with no vowel between un and šu; Harper normalizes accusative + -šu) “his ear”; the noun has no plural ending here, so one ear · noun · uznam (uz-na-am, accusative) “ear”, and by extension “understanding”: uznam u nēmeqam “understanding and wisdom”
glossary.warḫum: month (written with ITI, the moon-month sign): warḫim “of the month” · warḫušu (ITI-šu) “his month”, nominative with -šu (Harper normalizes arḫišu) · arḫī (the sign ITI written twice, ITI.ITI; the doubled sign marks the plural) “months”: ūmī arḫī šanāt palêšu “the days, months, years of his reign”
glossary.zamûm-Š: Š-stem of zamûm (Harper’s zamû III,1 “to deprive”; his glossary has no simple stem, so “to lack, be deprived” is inferred and UNCERTAIN): to deprive, taking two accusatives · lišazmi (li-ša-az-mi, Š precative) “let him deprive”: mê lišazmi “let him deprive (them) of water”
glossary.zumrum: body: zumrišu (zu-um-ri-šu) “his body”; ina zumrišu “in his body”
glossary.zunnum: rain (Harper’s zunnu): zunnī (zu-ni) “rains”, a plural form
glossary.ālum: city (URU): ālum u rabiānum “the city and the mayor”
glossary.Šamaš: Shamash ({d}UTU) — the sun-god, lord of justice
glossary.ša: who, which, of · also “whose”: ša + a noun with its own suffix + the verb at the end (ša ḫaṭṭašu išarat “whose scepter is straight”), the verb in the subjunctive
glossary.šadālum: to be wide; D-stem — mušaddil “who widens” · lišaddilšu (li-ša-ad-di-il-šu, precative + -šu, Harper’s šadālu II,1, D-stem, glossed by him “to extend, to multiply”) “let him increase (for him)”: kammal šarrūtim lišaddilšu “let him increase for him the burden of kingship”, UNCERTAIN
glossary.šakānum: to set, place: išakkanūšumma “they shall set for him (a term), and” · išakkanūšum (present, plural, dative -šum) “they shall place (it) for him”, i.e. count it to him · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be put”: ul iššakkan “it shall not be put (in the account)” · to set, put, impose: ištakan (iš-ta-ka-an, perfect, “has set”), išakkan (present) — išakkanšima (i-ša-ak-ka-an-ši-ma, with -ši and -ma) “he/she shall set (it) on her, and”, as in abbuttam išakkan · išakkanūši “they shall set (her on a stake)”, išakkanūšumma “they shall set (it) aside for him, and” · idiom panam šakānum (panam ištakan) “to set the face” = to make up one’s mind · iššakkan also written iš-ta-ak-ka-an (Harper’s reading, UNCERTAIN): andurār amtim iššakkan “the release of the slave-woman shall be established” · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be set”: andurāršunu iššakkan “their release shall be set” · šaknāt (ša-ak-na-at, feminine plural stative) “those set (with)”: šaknāt napištim “those set with life”, i.e. those who have life, UNCERTAIN · liškunšum (li-iš-ku-un-šum, G precative + -šum) “let him set for him”
glossary.šanānum: to rival (Harper’s šananu): šāninam (ša-ni-nam, accusative) “a rival”; the clause it stands in is UNCERTAIN · šitannu (ši-ta-an-nu, Harper’s šanānu I,2, a t-stem) “(a life which) is the match of (death)”, UNCERTAIN in form: balāṭam ša itti mūtim šitannu
glossary.šaplîš: below (adverb in -iš, from šaplum “lower part”): šaplîš (ša-ap-li-iš); with elîš “above”
glossary.šattum: year: šattam (syllabic, §31) or MU (the year-sign, §30) · šattim (genitive); plural šanātim “years” (ša šanātim “of the years”); MU 4{kam}, said erbe šanātim “four years” · MU 3{kam}, said šalāš šanātim “for three years”; šanat (ša-na-at) “(in) the year”, ina šanat “each year” · šanāt (ša-na-a-at) “the years of”, the plural construct before a genitive: šanāt palêšu “the years of his reign”
glossary.šâmum: to buy: ištām “he bought”, išammu “he buys” · ALSO a second verb of the same spelling, “to fix, decree” (destinies, well-being): išīm (i-ši-im) “he decreed”, išīmam (i-ši-ma-am) “he decreed for me” (preterite + the ventive -am) · lišīmšum (li-ši-im-šum, precative + -šum) “let him decree for him”: ana šīmtim lišīmšum “let him decree for him as fate”
glossary.šērtum: sword, scimitar (Harper’s šêrtu, the second of his two nouns of this spelling, glossed “sword, scimitar”; the sense UNCERTAIN): šērissu (še-ri-zu, with -šu, the t and š said ss, written ZU) “his sword”; perhaps a weapon of the moon-god · a different word from šērtum-sin
glossary.šērtum-sin: sin, guilt (Harper’s šêrtu “sin”, the first of his two nouns of this spelling): šērissu (še-ri-zu, with -šu) “his sin”, šērissu rabītam “his great sin” · a different word from šērtum “sword”
glossary.šīmtum: fate; one’s natural death: ana šīmtim ittalak “he went to (his) fate” = he died · plural šīmātum “fates”: šīmātīša (ši-ma-ti-ša) “her fates”; ina šīmātīša imtūt “she died in her fates” = she died a natural death
glossary.šīrum: flesh, body; wellbeing · šīr (SU, bound form before a genitive) “flesh of”: šīr pasuttišu “the flesh of its pasuttu” · šīram (written UZU, Harper’s List no. 80; the sign TENTATIVE) “omen, oracle” (Harper’s ŠÎRU “oracle”): šīram lemnam “an evil omen”
glossary.šūpûm: to make appear, make manifest (š-stem of wapûm) · šūpât (šu-pa-a-at, stative) “it shines forth, is made to appear” (Harper: “to shine”)
glossary.ūmum: day; ūmišu “daily” (written UD-mi-šu) · plural “days”: ūmī (written UD-mi-) “days”: ina ūmīšu lā malûtim “in his days not full” (the days of a lease) · ūm “day” (UD), before a following word, in ūm NER lā “a day (when ?) NER not …” · ūmīšu (UD-mi-šu) “his days”: ūmīšu imannûma “they shall count his days” · ina ūmim (i-na UD) “per day, by the day”, with the numeral 1{kam}: ina ūmim 1{kam} 180 qa “for each day 180 qa”; the day-rate formula of §271–277 · ūmī (the sign UD alone) “days”: ūmī iṣūtim “few days” · ūmī (UD-mi) “days” in a list with arḫī “months” and šanāt “years”; ūm (UD-um) “day(s) of” before a genitive: ūm balāṭīya “the days of my life”
glossary.ḫalāqum: to be lost, vanish: ḫalqu, ḫalqam · iḫtaliq (iḫ-ta-li-iq, perfect) “it has been lost”; ḫaliq (ḫa-li-iq, stative) “(it) is lost”, ḫaliqma “is lost, and”; lā ḫaliqma “is not lost, and” · ḫalāq (ḫa-la-aq, infinitive in the construct) “the loss of”: ḫalāq mātišu “the loss of his land” · iḫalliqu (i-ḫal-li-qu₂, present with the subjunctive -u) “(which) will vanish”: ša ina zumrišu lā iḫalliqu “which will not vanish in his body”
glossary.ḫalāqum-D: D-stem of ḫalāqum “to be lost, to perish”: to destroy, cause to be lost: uḫalliqu (preterite, with the relative -u) “(the grain) he destroyed” · uḫtalliq (uḫ-ta-al-li-iq, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has destroyed”: šumma makkūr uḫtalliq “if he has destroyed property”; of a boatman, ù lū uḫtalliq “or has destroyed (it)” · liḫalliq (li-ḫal-li-iq, precative with li-, as litēr; a D precative is normally lu-, so the form is UNCERTAIN) “let him destroy”: mātassu ... liḫalliq “let him destroy his land”
glossary.ḫalāṣum-Š: Š-stem of ḫalāṣum: to destroy (Harper’s ḫalṣû III,1) · lišḫelṣi (li-iš-ḫi-[el]-ṣi, Š precative) “let him destroy”, UNCERTAIN; the sign el is partly dotted on the plate, so Harper brackets [el]; the sign ZI is read ṣi
glossary.ḫegallum: abundance (Sumerian ḫé-gál, written with its own signs)
glossary.ḫušaḫḫum: hunger, famine (Harper’s ḫušaḫḫu): ḫušaḫḫim (ḫu-ša-aḫ-ḫi-im, genitive) in šanāt ḫušaḫḫim “years of famine”
